newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan reforms to regain market confidence-official.
newsitem.headline: Japan reforms to regain market confidence-official.

text.p: The Japanese government will do its best to implement various promises for reform and deregulation to restore the confidence of financial markets, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference on Friday.
"The confidence of the markets should increase if the Japanese government continues to make efforts to implement reforms."
Kajiyama said the government's view that the Japanese economy was in a recovery phase remained unchanged and said he did not understand why the financial markets were so pessimistic now.
"There is no immediate remedy (to raise share prices)," Kajiyama said. He said prices should go back up if Japan continued to strengthen its economic fundamentals through various reforms.

He made the comments after Japanese shares plummeted on Friday. The key Nikkei index of 225 leading shares marked a two-year closing low, capping a week of furious selling which analysts said was showing no signs of abating.

The Nikkei 225 tumbled 770.22 points, or 4.26 percent, to close at 17,303.65, its lowest close since August 1995. The day's fall took the Nikkei's losses in the first week of the new year to 2,057.7 points.
